materialization_contract.scalar_xor: JavaScript ToInt32 operands/result, immediately materialized lane-wise by cpu_uvec3 as >>> 0
materialization_contract.float32: typed bindings and Surface stores use Math.fround/Float32Array materialization
materialization_contract.round: canonical CPU runtime uses Math.round; positive ties go toward +Infinity; negative half can produce -0 before clamp/int materialization
materialization_contract.amount_alias: Grain exposes alpha; this oracle labels it amount only as a cross-port semantic alias
materialization_contract.noise_scale_alias: Grain reads infrastructure renderScale and clamps it to at least 1; there is no effect-level noiseScale parameter
materialization_contract.colored_mode: unreachable: canonical Grain has no colored control and broadcasts one scalar noise_value to RGB
materialization_contract.external_seed_and_frame: unreachable in the render: canonical Grain uses BASE_SEED=0x1234 and reads neither binding

unreachable_traps: External seed and frame omission cannot be a pixel mutation witness because this canonical program does not read either binding; paired renders prove identity.
A signed scalar XOR result and its immediate cpu_uvec3 unsigned materialization have identical low 32 bits; the authenticated parent role is structural, not pixel-observable.

Negative-half and negative-zero round distinctions are erased by max(..., 0), integer materialization, and max(as_u32(...), 1) before any render coordinate uses them; direct round evidence freezes the intermediate behavior.
There is no colored/monochrome branch to toggle. A mutation that breaks the fixed scalar-to-RGB broadcast is required to diverge instead.
